chunks: Muḥammad ibn Qays narrated from one of the two Imams, peace be upon them:
Concerning a man who gouged out another man's eye, cut off his nose and his ears, then killed him.

He, peace be upon him, said: "If he inflicted that upon him separately, retaliation is taken from him, then he is killed. But if he struck him with a single blow and that resulted in it, his neck is struck, and retaliation is not taken from him."

key_terms.ضُرِبَتْ عُنُقُهُ: his neck is struck, meaning he is executed
key_terms.قَطَعَ أَنْفَهُ وَ أُذُنَيْهِ: cutting off the victim's nose and ears

ai.seo_question: When are separate acts of qisas carried out before execution in a murder case involving multiple injuries?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on retaliation and execution when multiple grave injuries are followed by murder. If the injuries were inflicted separately, qisas applies for the injuries before execution; if they all resulted from a single blow, only execution is carried out without separate retaliation for each injury.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5280 - Muhammad ibn Qays narrated from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them)
about a man who gouged out another man's eye, cut off his nose and ears, and then killed him.

Imam (as) said: "If he inflicted these injuries on him separately, then retaliation (qisas) will be taken for each injury, and then he will be killed. But if he struck him with a single blow that resulted in all those injuries, his neck will be struck (he will be executed), and retaliation will not be taken for the individual injuries."
